resultJson.description:
Spotify can issue a new refresh token at the browser sign-in and on every renewal, but `SpotifyClient` only keeps it in its `Ref[F, Option[SpotifySession]]`. After a restart the app goes back to SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN, which may be stale by then, or asks for another browser sign-in. This epic saves the newest refresh token Spotify has issued in one owner-only file (0600, in a directory the app creates 0700) and starts from it next time. The start-up order becomes: saved token, then SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN, then the browser. So after one browser sign-in, restarts on a home machine, a Pi or in Docker need no further action.

The design comes from `docs/adr/0002-save-the-newest-spotify-refresh-token-in-an-owner.md`, and its program design is followed except for three changes:
- `FileModes[F]` gains `creationModes(perms): Option[Permissions]`, so a test can reach the branch where a file is created on a filesystem without POSIX permissions. Otherwise that branch can't be tested on Linux tmp, and criterion 9 would go unproven.
- `TokenStore.file(path, modes)` delegates to a `private[client]` overload that also takes the move and delete operations. Tests can then make a move or a delete fail, which otherwise needs a special filesystem or a non-root user.
- The once-per-run WARN dedupe covers load-side problems too, so a loose file on vfat gives one "couldn't restrict" WARN per run, not one at load and another at save.

The pieces:
- A pure `TokenFile` works out the path: SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE, then `spotify.token-file`, then `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token`, then `$HOME/.config/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token`, with blank counting as unset. It also handles the file format: the token, as ASCII graphic characters, plus one `\n`.
- A `TokenStore[F]` (load/save/forget) does the I/O. It reads the file once when built. It saves atomically through a same-directory temp file created 0600 and then moved. It checks permissions by reading them back through `FileModes[F]`.
- Every problem with the file is a `TokenFileProblem`, logged once as a WARN and never raised, so the token file can never stop the app from starting or keep it from running.
- `SpotifyClient` gets the store as one more constructor parameter. It loads the saved token first and forgets it on invalid_grant. It saves every refresh token Spotify issues, and `renew` with no session goes through `signIn`.
- `Main` builds the store from the config plus `Env`.

No log line may contain the token's value, at any level and including the WARNs. Every behaviour criterion needs a test that fails without the change. The tests use munit with ScalaCheck and `CatsEffectSuite`, a fake Spotify over HTTP, real files in `Files[IO].tempDirectory`, and logback `ListAppender` capture with the `client` loggers lowered to TRACE. The README, .env.example and docs carry the documentation criteria, and no test reads them. `sbt check` has to pass at the end of every task: 90% of statements and 85% of branches overall, 70% of statements in each file, and the Scalafix rules, none of which may be relaxed.

tasks.title: Token file location, format and problems (TokenFile, TokenFileProblem, spotify.token-file)
tasks.description:
Add the pure pieces from ADR 0002's program design.

- New `src/main/scala/client/TokenFileProblem.scala`: `enum TokenFileProblem derives CanEqual` with the cases Unreadable(path, reason), Empty(path), Malformed(path), LoosePermissions(path), NoPosixPermissions(path), Unwritable(path, reason), Undeletable(path, reason) and NoLocation.
  - `message: String` gives the WARN texts listed under Observability in the ADR: "Couldn't read the saved refresh token", "The saved refresh token file is empty", "The saved refresh token file is malformed", "The refresh token file was readable by others; restricted it to 0600", "Couldn't restrict the refresh token file's permissions on this filesystem", "Couldn't save the refresh token", "Couldn't delete or empty the rejected refresh token file" and "No location for the refresh token file; keeping it in memory".
  - Add `context: Map[String, String]`: "path" for every case except NoLocation, and "reason" where the case has one. The store logs `logger.warn(problem.context)(problem.message)`.
  - Messages and context never include file contents.
- New `src/main/scala/client/TokenFile.scala`: `object TokenFile` with `val EnvVar = "SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE"` and three functions.
  - `locate(configured: Option[String], env: Map[String,String]): Option[fs2.io.file.Path]`. The order is env SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE, then configured, then `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token`, then `HOME/.config/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token`. Blank or whitespace-only values count as unset, and the result is None when there is nothing to go on.
  - `parse(path, contents): Either[TokenFileProblem, String]`.
    - Empty or whitespace-only contents give `Empty(path)`.
    - Otherwise, remove one trailing "\n". What remains must be non-empty and contain only ASCII graphic characters (0x21 to 0x7E), or the result is `Malformed(path)`.
    - Use ASCII only, because fs2's `readUtf8` turns invalid bytes into U+FFFD, which `Character`-based "printable" checks accept.
  - `render(token): String` returns the token plus "\n".
- `src/main/scala/domain/spotify/SpotifyCredentials.scala`: add `tokenFile: Option[String] = None` as the last field. pureconfig maps `token-file` to it, and the circe codec gains an optional field. Change nothing else.
- Tests:
  - New `src/test/scala/client/TokenFileSpec.scala` (a ScalaCheckSuite).
    - A table for `locate` covers env, config, XDG, HOME, blank values and none at all, including SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE beating the config value.
    - A ScalaCheck round-trip shows `parse(render(t)) == Right(t)` for generated tokens over 0x21 to 0x7E.
    - A table of empty, whitespace-only, multi-line, embedded-space, control-character, U+FFFD and non-ASCII (for example "töken") contents expects Empty or Malformed.
    - `render` is exactly the token plus one newline.
    - No problem's `message` or `context` contains a token.
  - In `src/test/scala/domain/config/LightShowConfigSpec.scala`, which already loads `AppConfig` from `required` with the `reference.conf` fallback through its `load` helper, check two things. Loading with `spotify.token-file = "/x"` gives `spotify.tokenFile == Some("/x")`. Without it the value is None.

Covers criteria 4, 5 (path resolution and precedence) and 6 (format).

tasks.title: FileModes and TokenStore: owner-only, atomic, read-once token file
tasks.description:
Implement `src/main/scala/client/FileModes.scala` and `src/main/scala/client/TokenStore.scala` as ADR 0002 describes, with the changes below. The ADR's Failure modes and Observability sections give the exact behaviour. The logger is `Slf4jLogger.getLogger[F]` in `TokenStore`, so its name is `client.TokenStore`.

`FileModes[F]` has three methods:
- `get(path): F[PosixPermissions]`.
- `set(path, perms): F[Unit]`.
- `creationModes(perms: PosixPermissions): Option[Permissions]`. This one is added to the ADR's trait. It gives the attributes to create a file or directory with. A fake returns None, so tests can reach the branch where a filesystem stores no permissions.

`FileModes.posix[F: Files]` wraps `Files[F].getPosixPermissions` and `setPosixPermissions`, and its `creationModes` is `Some(perms)`.

`TokenStore` has `none` and `at`, as the ADR describes, and `file` built on a package-private overload:
- `none[F: Applicative]` keeps nothing: load gives None, save and forget do nothing.
- `at[F: Async: Files](location)`:
  - None: log WARN NoLocation and return `none`.
  - Some(path): log INFO "Spotify refresh token file" {path}, then call `file(path, FileModes.posix)`.
- `file(path, modes)` delegates to `private[client] def file(path, modes, move: (Path, Path) => F[Unit], delete: Path => F[Unit])`. The defaults are `Files[F].move(_, _, CopyFlags(CopyFlag.AtomicMove, CopyFlag.ReplaceExisting))` and `Files[F].delete`. This seam is a change from the ADR, so that tests can reach the move and delete fallbacks.
- One `Ref[F, Set[problem kind]]` dedupes WARNs for the whole store, load and save alike. Every WARN goes through "log if this kind hasn't been logged yet". The once-per-kind rule applies to NoPosixPermissions and Unwritable, and Undeletable can use it too. A NoPosixPermissions logged at load is therefore never logged again by a later save.

Load happens once, inside `file`, and `load` returns the result from a `Ref`:
- A missing file gives None with no log.
- Unreadable gives one WARN and None. A token path that is a directory is one example; its reason is the exception's class and message.
- Empty and Malformed (from `TokenFile.parse`) each give one WARN and None.
- For a token that parses, check the mode with `modes.get`:
  - If `get` throws, log a NoPosixPermissions WARN and still use the token.
  - If any group or other bit is set, call `modes.set(path, 0600)` and read the mode back with `get`. If the read-back is exactly 0600, log a LoosePermissions WARN. If it isn't, or if set or get throws, log a NoPosixPermissions WARN. Either way, use the token.
  - Never treat a permissions failure as Unreadable.

`save(token)` is serialised by `cats.effect.std.Mutex` and never raises:
- Create the parent directories with `modes.creationModes(0700)`. If that throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, retry with None and record NoPosixPermissions; this does not make the save unwritable.
- Create a temp file in the same directory with `modes.creationModes(0600)`. Handle `UnsupportedOperationException` the same way: retry with None, record NoPosixPermissions, and carry on writing.
- Write `TokenFile.render(token)` to the temp file, then `move` it over the target.
- If the move fails, write the target in place with `Flags.Write` (truncate), then delete the temp file.
- Then read the permissions back with `modes.get`. Anything other than 0600, or an exception, means NoPosixPermissions. The file stays written either way.
- Only an IO failure in mkdir, the temp write or the fallback write is Unwritable {path, reason}, where reason is the exception's class and message. Clean up the temp file if one was created. The token stays in memory.

`forget` never raises:
- Call `delete(path)`. If that fails, truncate the file to empty. Log Undeletable {path, reason} only if both fail.
- Clear the loaded token either way.

Tests go in a new `src/test/scala/client/TokenStoreSpec.scala`, using `Files[IO].tempDirectory` and the real fs2 `Files`. Logs come from `Tls.capturedLogs` under `Tls.loggingAt("client", Level.TRACE)`, counting WARNs from `client.TokenStore`.
- A file the app creates is 0600 and a directory it creates is 0700, read with the real `getPosixPermissions`.
- An existing 0644 file ends up 0600, gives exactly one LoosePermissions WARN, and load returns its token.
- Three fakes give exactly one NoPosixPermissions WARN, never the "restricted it to 0600" WARN, and the token is still loaded or the file still written:
  - `set` does nothing, so `get` keeps returning 0644;
  - `set` throws IOException;
  - `get` throws at load.
- A fake whose `creationModes` returns None, so files are created without attributes and `get` doesn't report 0600: the file is written with the token plus a newline, there is exactly one NoPosixPermissions WARN across several saves, and there is no Unwritable WARN.
- A loose file loaded through a fake that can't restrict, then saved to: exactly one NoPosixPermissions WARN in total.
- A `move` that fails: the target still ends up holding exactly the new token plus a newline, and no temp file is left behind.
- `forget` deletes the file, and afterwards `load` gives None.
- A `delete` that fails: the file is truncated to empty, there is no Undeletable WARN, and a new store on that path loads None with an Empty WARN.
- A `delete` that fails on a path that is a directory, so it can't be truncated either: exactly one Undeletable WARN.
- A parent path that is a regular file makes the save unwritable: exactly one WARN naming the path and the reason across several saves, and no error raised.
- A token path that is a directory is unreadable: one WARN, load gives None.
- Empty and malformed files give one WARN each, and load gives None. A missing file gives no WARN.
- Parallel saves (`parTraverse`) leave exactly one of the tokens plus a newline, and no temp files.
- `at(None)` gives exactly one NoLocation WARN and a store that keeps nothing.
- A ScalaCheck property, or a forAll over generated tokens, across these scenarios: no captured event's message, MDC value or throwable message contains the token.

Covers the store side of criteria 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 and 13.

tasks.title: SpotifyClient starts from, saves and forgets the saved refresh token; Main builds the store
tasks.description:
Apply the ADR 0002 diff to `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala` and `src/main/scala/Main.scala` together. Changing the signature of `SpotifyClient.resource` breaks the call at `Main.scala:31` otherwise.

SpotifyClient constructors:
- The primary constructor gains `store: TokenStore[F]` as its last parameter.
- Add a 4-argument constructor `(client, creds, session, codes: SignInCodes[F])` that uses `TokenStore.none[F]`. `SpotifyClientSpec:188` and `:282` and `SyncEngineRunSpec:349` use this shape.
- The existing `Deferred` constructor also passes `TokenStore.none[F]`.
- `SpotifyClient.resource(client, creds, store)` passes the store on.

SpotifyClient behaviour:
- `signIn`:
  - Call `store.load`.
  - On Some(saved): call `refreshWith("Refresh Token Exchange", saved)`, then log INFO "Signed in to Spotify with the saved refresh token" {client_id}.
  - On `SpotifyTokenError.Rejected`: log WARN "Spotify rejected the saved refresh token (status: …); deleted it and falling back" {client_id}, call `store.forget`, then `fromConfigured`.
  - On None: go straight to `fromConfigured`.
  - `Failed` (429, 5xx) propagates and the file is kept.
- `fromConfigured` is the old `signIn` body: the configured token, with the browser fallback on Rejected, keeping its existing log lines.
- `renew` with no session calls `signIn`.
- `refreshWith` calls `store.save(newToken)` when Spotify's answer has a `refresh_token`.
- `initialAuth` calls `store.save(refresh)` after the code exchange.
- Keep the existing code style in this file (colon-bodied class), and change nothing else.

Main changes:
- Import `cats.effect.std.Env` and `client.{TokenFile, TokenStore}`.
- Add `env <- Resource.eval(Env[IO].entries.map(_.toMap))` and `store <- Resource.eval(TokenStore.at[IO](TokenFile.locate(config.spotify.tokenFile, env)))`, and pass `store` to `SpotifyClient.resource`. Main is excluded from coverage.

Keeping MainSpec hermetic (required):
- `MainSpec` runs `Main.start` with the real `HttpClients`. Without a fix it would read the developer's real `~/.config/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token` and send the token to accounts.spotify.com.
- In `build.sbt`, next to `Test / envVars += "SPOTIFY_SP_DC" -> "sp-dc-sentinel"`, add `Test / envVars += "SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE" -> (target.value / "test-refresh-token" / "refresh-token").getAbsolutePath`, or an equivalent absolute path under `target`.
- Setting it in MainSpec's HOCON isn't enough, because an exported SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE would win.
- Don't touch the coverage settings.

Tests: add a new spec `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyTokenFileSpec.scala`.
- The fake Spotify over HTTP records each refresh_token sent, in the style of `SpotifyClientSpec.rig`. Every token in a scenario is distinct.
- To simulate a restart, each start builds a fresh `TokenStore.file(path, FileModes.posix[IO])`, a fresh session `Ref`, `SignInCodes` and `SpotifyClient` on the same temp path. A store is never reused across starts, because `load` returns what the file held when that store was built.
- Use `TestControl.executeEmbed` for the browser wait.

Scenarios:
- A browser sign-in, then a second start with no configured token, signs in with one refresh_token call that sends the issued token, and logs no "Please visit".
- A renewal whose answer carries a new refresh_token: the file then holds exactly that token plus a newline, and the next start's first token call sends it.
- A saved token beats a different configured token, both from `getPlaybackState` and when `renew` is the first call.
- A saved token answered with 400 invalid_grant gives the WARN and removes the file. It then sends the configured token, or opens the browser sign-in when none is configured. A third start never sends the rejected token.
- A malformed file, then a configured token answered 503 twice with sign-in retried: exactly one Malformed WARN, and both polls fail with `SpotifyTokenError.Failed` rather than crashing the app.
- A token path whose parent is a regular file: exactly one Unwritable WARN across several renewals, and the polls keep succeeding.
- A ScalaCheck property, or a forAll, over generated tokens runs these scenarios under `Tls.loggingAt("client", Level.TRACE)`. That covers `client.SpotifyClient` and `client.TokenStore` at every level, since root is WARN in logback-test.xml. It asserts that no captured event's message, MDC value or throwable message contains the token.

The existing SpotifyClientSpec, SpotifyRenewSpec, SyncEngineRunSpec and MainSpec tests must keep passing unchanged.

Covers criteria 1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 12 and 13 end to end.

tasks.title: Document the saved refresh token
tasks.description:
Documentation and config comments only. No tests; these files meet criteria 14 and 15 themselves.

- `src/main/resources/application.conf`: inside `spotify { … }`, add a commented `# token-file = "/data/refresh-token"` with a one-line note that SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE overrides it. Don't use `${?…}`: the ADR explains that a later user line would then beat the variable.
- `README.md`: add a SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE row to the Configuration table (lines 19-27), and update the SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN row. Add a short section explaining:
  - where the refresh token is saved by default ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token, or ~/.config/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token)
  - how to move it with `spotify.token-file` or SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE, and that the variable wins
  - that the saved token beats SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN
  - that deleting the file makes the app fall back to SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN and then the browser sign-in, which is how to switch token or account
  - that the file is owner-only
- `.env.example`: add `SPOTIFY_TOKEN_FILE=` with a comment that it is optional and defaults to ~/.config/spotify-hue-sync/refresh-token (or under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME). An empty value counts as unset.
- `docs/how-it-works.md`, Spotify sign-in section (lines ~10-33): update the sequence diagram and bullets for the saved-token-first order, saving on the code exchange and on renewal, and forgetting the saved token on invalid_grant.
- `docs/architecture.md`: add `TokenStore`, `TokenFile` and `FileModes` to the `client` package row (line 64), and mention building the store in the startup sequence.

resultJson.brief:
## What exists
- Build: sbt with Scala 3.9.0 and `-indent`. The root module is `.` (the app) plus `model/` (cross JVM/JS) and `ui/` (Scala.js).
- Libraries: cats-effect 3.6.3, fs2(-io) 3.12.2, http4s 0.23.33 Ember, circe 0.14.15, pureconfig 0.17.10 (`pureconfig-generic-scala3`), log4cats-slf4j 2.7.1 and logback 1.5.32. Tests use munit 1.0.0, munit-scalacheck, munit-cats-effect 2.0.0 and cats-effect-testkit.
- Tests run forked (`Test / fork := true`). `Test / envVars` sets SPOTIFY_SP_DC=sp-dc-sentinel (`build.sbt:104-105`), and the forked JVM also inherits the shell's environment.
- Coverage minimums: 90% of statements and 85% of branches overall, 70% of statements per file. `coverageExcludedPackages` (`build.sbt:92`) covers `Main;audio.AudioCapture;client.DtlsEmitter;beat.BeatTracking`. Don't change any of this.
- `sbt fix` applies rewrites and formatting; `sbt check` is what CI runs.
- Scalafix (`.scalafix.conf`) forbids:
  - nulls, `isInstanceOf` and `return`;
  - `implicit` (use given/using/summon);
  - a `cats.implicits` import (use `cats.syntax.all.*`);
  - unsafeRun or the global runtime outside Main.

  Tests have their own rules in `.scalafix.test.conf`; prefer `CatsEffectSuite`. Enums need `derives CanEqual`. DirectoryAndPackageName and FileNameConsistent apply, so `client/Foo.scala` must declare `package client` and define `Foo`. Catch exceptions with `NonFatal` (the ThrowableToNonFatal rule).
- Style:
  - New code uses braces, not colon blocks. `SpotifyClient.scala` itself is colon-bodied (`class …:`, `for … yield`), so keep that file's style when editing it.
  - Comment only what the code can't say.
  - Test names say what is checked, with no comments in tests.
  - Make the smallest change at the point of the problem.

## Design
- The design is in `docs/adr/0002-save-the-newest-spotify-refresh-token-in-an-owner.md`, with exact signatures, log texts, failure modes and the Main/SpotifyClient diffs. Read it first.
- Agreed changes from the ADR, which the PR should mention:
  1. `FileModes` gains `creationModes(perms: PosixPermissions): Option[Permissions]` (`posix` gives Some), so a creation without POSIX attributes is testable.
  2. `TokenStore.file(path, modes)` delegates to a `private[client]` overload that also takes `move: (Path, Path) => F[Unit]` and `delete: Path => F[Unit]`, so the move and delete fallbacks are testable.
  3. The once-per-kind WARN dedupe `Ref` covers load and save together, so there is at most one NoPosixPermissions WARN per run.

  `TokenFile.parse` accepts ASCII graphic characters (0x21 to 0x7E) only. This makes the ADR's \"printable characters with no spaces\" precise, because `readUtf8` decodes bad bytes as U+FFFD.

## Files
- `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala`. Today the class takes `(client: Client[F], creds: SpotifyCredentials, session: Ref[F, Option[SpotifySession]], codes: SignInCodes[F])`. There is also a secondary constructor taking `authCode: Deferred[F,String]`, which uses `SignInCodes.once`.
  - `initialAuth: F[String]`:
    - logs \"Please visit: <url>\" and waits for `codes.attempt`;
    - POSTs authorization_code to `authUri`, and raises if the answer has no `refresh_token`;
    - sets the session and logs INFO \"Signed in to Spotify through the browser\" with MDC `Map(\"client_id\" -> creds.clientId)`.
  - `signIn` = `creds.configuredRefreshToken.fold(initialAuth)(refreshWith(\"Refresh Token Exchange\", _) … recoverWith { case SpotifyTokenError.Rejected(_, status, _) => warn … *> initialAuth })`.
  - `getOrRefresh` signs in when there is no session. `renew`'s no-session branch currently uses configured-or-initialAuth.
  - `private refreshWith(call, refresh)` POSTs grant_type=refresh_token and sets the session to `SpotifySession(access, resp.refresh_token.getOrElse(refresh))`.
  - `authorised` retries once after a 401, through `renew`.
  - `SpotifyClient.resource(client, creds)` builds the Ref, `SignInCodes.make` and the callback server on 127.0.0.1:7070.
  - Logging uses `Slf4jLogger.getLogger[F]`, so the logger name is the class name, `client.SpotifyClient`. Structured MDC goes through `logger.warn(ctxMap)(msg)`.
- `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyTokenError.scala`: `enum SpotifyTokenError extends RuntimeException { Rejected(call, status, body); Failed(call, status, body) }`. `SpotifyTokenError.of` gives Rejected only for 400 with error=invalid_grant. Its messages never contain the token.
- `src/main/scala/client/SignInCodes.scala`: `attempt: F[F[String]]`, `hand(code): F[Boolean]`, `once(deferred)` and `make[F: Concurrent]`.
- `src/main/scala/domain/spotify/SpotifyCredentials.scala`: `case class SpotifyCredentials(clientId, clientSecret, refreshToken: Option[String] = None) derives Codec.AsObject`, with `configuredRefreshToken` (trimmed; blank counts as None).
- `src/main/scala/domain/config/AppConfig.scala`: `AppConfig derives ConfigReader`, and kebab-case keys map automatically, so `token-file` maps to `tokenFile`. `AppConfig.load[F](source)`.
- `src/test/scala/domain/config/LightShowConfigSpec.scala`: has `required` HOCON, `reference = ConfigSource.resources(\"reference.conf\")` and `load(extra): Either[String, AppConfig]` at lines 15-18.
- `src/main/scala/Main.scala`: `start(source)` builds one Resource, and line 31 is `SpotifyClient.resource[IO](clients.spotify, config.spotify)`. `MainSpec` calls `Main.start` with real HttpClients against fake bridges.
- `src/main/resources/application.conf`: the `spotify {}` block holds client-id, client-secret and `refresh-token = ${?SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN}`. `reference.conf` gets no default for token-file.
- Docs: `.env.example` is a plain list of `KEY=` lines. The `README.md` Configuration table is at lines 19-27. The sign-in section of `docs/how-it-works.md` is at lines ~10-33, and the `client` row of the package table in `docs/architecture.md` is at line 64.

## Test infrastructure
- `src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala`:
  - `Tls.capturedLogs: Resource[IO, ListAppender[ILoggingEvent]]` is attached to the root logger.
  - `Tls.logged(appender): List[ILoggingEvent]`.
  - `Tls.loggingAt(name, Level)` temporarily sets one logger's level.
  - `src/test/resources/logback-test.xml` sets root to WARN. Use `Tls.loggingAt(\"client\", Level.TRACE)` to see every level from `client.SpotifyClient` and `client.TokenStore`; the no-token checks need this.
  - Events have `getFormattedMessage`, `getLevel`, `getLoggerName`, `getMDCPropertyMap` and `getThrowableProxy`.
- `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyClientSpec.scala` patterns to copy:
  - `rig(clientId, configured, answer)` is a fake token endpoint recording `TokenCall(grant, refreshToken, code)`.
  - `renewedTo(access, Some(refresh))` builds a JSON token answer, and `playerFor` accepts Bearer \"signed-in\".
  - `browserSignIn(r)` starts a poll, sleeps 1s, hands a code through `SpotifyClient.callbackRoutes(codes)` and joins; it runs under `TestControl.executeEmbed`.
  - Helpers `visits`, `infoLines` and `warnings`, and a no-token check over message, MDC values and throwable message.
  - Fake HTTP is `Client.fromHttpApp(HttpRoutes.of[IO]{ case req @ POST -> Root / \"api\" / \"token\" => … }.orNotFound)`. Path matching ignores the host.
- A simulated restart needs a new `TokenStore.file(...)`, a new session Ref and a new client on the same path. Never reuse a store across starts.

## fs2 / CE APIs (check exact signatures in fs2 3.12)
- `fs2.io.file.{Files, Path, Permissions, PosixPermissions, PosixPermission, Flags, Flag, CopyFlags, CopyFlag}`:
  - `Files[F].createDirectories(path, permissions: Option[Permissions])`
  - `Files[F].createTempFile(dir: Option[Path], prefix, suffix, permissions: Option[Permissions])`
  - `Files[F].move(src, dst, CopyFlags(CopyFlag.AtomicMove, CopyFlag.ReplaceExisting))`
  - `getPosixPermissions(path)` and `setPosixPermissions(path, perms)`
  - `readUtf8(path)` and `writeUtf8(path, Flags.Write)` (create, truncate, write)
  - `delete`, `deleteIfExists`, `exists`, `isDirectory`, `isRegularFile`, `list`, `tempDirectory: Resource`
  - `PosixPermissions.fromOctal(\"600\")`, which returns an Option, or `PosixPermissions(PosixPermission.OwnerRead, PosixPermission.OwnerWrite)`
- On a filesystem without POSIX permissions (vfat, CIFS), creating with POSIX attributes throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, and `getPosixPermissions` may throw too. chmod can also silently do nothing, which is why only a read-back counts.
- The umask only removes bits, so 0600 and 0700 survive creation.
- `cats.effect.std.Mutex[F]`: `Mutex[F]` gives `F[Mutex[F]]`, then `mutex.lock.surround(fa)`.
- `cats.effect.std.Env[IO].entries`, and `Ref` for the read-once token and the WARN dedupe.

## Non-obvious points
- Tests may run as root in a container, where permission-based unwritable or undeletable setups don't hold. Use structural failures and the move/delete seams instead:
  - a parent path that is a regular file is unwritable;
  - a token path that is a directory is unreadable, and can't be deleted or truncated.
- `load` returns what the file held at construction (or None after `forget`), not what was saved later in the run, as the ADR specifies. So a broken file WARNs once per run even when the poller retries `signIn`.
- Permission problems never stop the token being used or saved. Only a real IO failure writing the file counts as Unwritable.
- `renew` with no session must go through `signIn`, so the saved token also wins when `renew` is the first call. That branch's call name becomes \"Refresh Token Exchange\". The specs that check the \"Renew\" name (SpotifyRenewSpec, SpotifyTlsSpec:100) all start with a session, so none depend on it.
- The secondary constructors with 4 arguments must stay, because the existing specs use them and get `TokenStore.none`.
- The MDC `reason` is `s\"${e.getClass.getName}: ${e.getMessage}\"`, never file contents. No token in any message, MDC value or exception message.
- Never print, log or commit `.env`.
